sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow scope/claim escalation beyond the upstream authorization intent and broker policy; exchanging a minimally-scoped token must not yield a token with additional claims/permissions.

sequences.description: Send an unsigned request object (alg=none) to the auth endpoint to attempt parameter injection (scope/audience/redirect). Expect explicit rejection or non-processing; acceptance with attacker-controlled parameters could violate authorization binding.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization parameters (scope/audience/redirect) must be bound to broker policy and authenticated request semantics; unsigned request objects must not be accepted/processed to grant elevated permissions.

sequences.description: Token exchange: use a subject_token minted for one audience, then request a different audience in RFC8693 exchange; Dex should reject or not mint a token usable for that audience.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must bind exchanged tokens to the upstream intent and client trust; a subject_token for audience A must not be exchangeable into a token for audience B unless explicitly allowed by broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to audience binding enforcement.

sequences.description: Cross-identity splicing: user_A obtains an upstream token; user_B (different principal) attempts to exchange user_A's subject_token while authenticating as the same client. Dex should not allow this to grant user_B a session for user_A or otherwise exceed upstream intent.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions/identity in the exchanged session must be bound to the upstream subject_token principal and broker policy; a different user must not be able to exchange someone else's token to gain their effective access.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition failed: test identities are not distinct, cannot evaluate cross-identity splicing.

sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Claims/permissions in the resulting session must be bounded by the requested scopes (upstream intent) and broker policy; requesting minimal scope should not yield extra claims like groups/profile.
